text:
Leo Carlsson was turning into Anaheim's go-to player, 29 points in 24 games at age 21, before an upper-body injury on Nov. 21 against Utah ended his night after six minutes. CBS Sports listed him day-to-day, and RotoWire reported he was ruled out again on Wednesday. It lands on a Ducks team that had already lost Beckett Sennecke to injured reserve.

His season has leaned heavily on the power play, where 19 of his points came, and Anaheim gets fewer than half of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice. His last ten games brought eight points against the 11.1 we'd expect at his ice time, so he was cooling before he got hurt. The tools are clear: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 73% of his entries last season, and NHL Edge puts his burst count in the 98th percentile. Our numbers project about 87 points. Watch how fast he gets back to 20 minutes a night.
headline: Carlsson's breakout pauses for an injury
